destination.title: Holographic cosmology: backgrounds, scalar descriptions and conditional consistency
destination.question: How do the supplied holographic cosmological models construct dark-sector or inflationary backgrounds, represent them with effective scalars, and confront their own observational or conjectural conditions?
destination.summary: Cutoff-based HDE and its entropy modifications provide the main connection. Induced holographic fluids, hidden-environment stabilization and inflationary applications retain separate homes. Shared holographic language does not identify their dynamics or establish quantum-gravity consistency.

systems: Conventional and entropy-modified holographic dark energy
Effective quintessence, dilaton and tachyon representations
An induced holographic dark fluid on a hypersurface
Holographically motivated inflation and late-time coasting
targets: Background evolution and source-dated observational comparisons
Adopted scalar-excursion, swampland and TCC tests
Proposed radiative stabilization and entropic cosmological selection
regimes: Late-time cosmology and selected past-to-present intervals
Flat and curved backgrounds where explicitly considered
Present and future scalar-potential tests where distinguished
assumptions: Cutoff choices, entropy laws, interactions and conjectures are source-local hypotheses.
Background scalar matching does not establish microscopic equivalence.
Different systems, dimensions and cosmological epochs may share this navigational family.
conventions: Preserve paper-specific Planck normalization, curvature signs and scalar branches.
Do not identify similarly named parameters across models.
Observational statements retain their source dates and datasets.
includes: Description-supported questions with explicit reading limits
Adjacent mechanisms and inflationary applications through separate overview cards
excludes: A universal holographic mechanism or common scalar theory
Sufficiency of an excursion or TCC test for ultraviolet consistency
Independent certification of reported fits, stability claims or full cosmological viability

sources.title: Cosmological Imprints of the Second Law of Thermodynamics

evidence.text: How does an assumed nondecreasing cosmological event-horizon area constrain holographic dark energy, the inflation-to-acceleration history, and observational determination of its dimensionless parameter d?

sources.title: Emergent Dark Universe and the Swampland Criteria

evidence.text: Can an induced holographic stress tensor reproduce the observed late-time expansion with only ordinary matter, and what do conjectural quantum-gravity constraints imply for a scalar potential reconstructed from that stress tensor?

evidence.text: What tachyon-field dynamics can represent Barrow holographic dark energy in flat or curved FRW backgrounds with and without dark-sector interactions, and what background evolution, inflationary expressions and TCC conditions follow within the chosen phenomenological setup?

sources.title: Holographic dark energy in a coasting cosmology

evidence.text: Can a late-time coasting universe satisfy the Trans-Planckian Censorship Conjecture and be supported by holographic dark energy constrained through horizon entropy, while accommodating independently evolving matter and the supplied low-redshift observations?

sources.title: Cosmological Imprints of the Second Law of Thermodynamics

evidence.text: Use Ωh, or y=1/√Ωh, to parameterize late evolution, matching the integration constant through continuity at radiation–dark-energy equality. Expand the implicit solution in the matter-dominated and dark-energy-dominated limits.

sources.title: Emergent Dark Universe and the Swampland Criteria

evidence.text: Reconstruct a scalar trajectory from a conserved fluid, fix its orientation and origin, and eliminate time to obtain a potential. The paper applies this operation to hEDU and sDGP before evaluating swampland diagnostics.

sources.title: Lagrangian Reconstruction of Barrow Holographic Dark Energy in Interacting Tachyon Model

evidence.text: Inflation uses L⁻²=αH²+βḢ, integrates the background equation in e-folds N, and constructs a slow-roll hierarchy. The imported TCC requirement is L_p/a_i<H_f⁻¹/a_f; the authors formally substitute their end-of-inflation Hubble expression to obtain a parameter bound.

sources.title: Holographic dark energy in a coasting cosmology

evidence.text: Parameter inference uses MCMC with emcee and combinations of Pantheon+ supernovae, DESI/SDSS BAO, angular BAO and 32 cosmic-chronometer points. The paper reports full covariance matrices for Pantheon+, standard BAO and CC, diagonal angular-BAO errors, and AIC/BIC/KIC comparisons with ΛCDM.

sources.title: Cosmological Imprints of the Second Law of Thermodynamics

evidence.text: Solve the Friedmann equation separately in the three phases and match quantities at their boundaries. Radiation-plus-matter evolution is treated exactly within its truncated energy content; the matter-plus-holographic-dark-energy phase uses previously published implicit solutions.

sources.title: Emergent Dark Universe and the Swampland Criteria

evidence.text: Map a parameterized expansion history into distance predictions, construct covariance-weighted observational residuals, add an external Gaussian expansion-scale constraint, and sample parameters. In this paper the operation compares hEDU with flat LCDM.

sources.title: A Model of holographic dark energy

evidence.text: Can a holographic ultraviolet–infrared cutoff relation produce accelerating dark energy with a predictive equation of state, and can inflation explain its present abundance relative to matter?

sources.title: Tsallis holographic dark energy for inflation

evidence.text: Can Tsallis holographic dark energy with a Granda–Oliveros cutoff drive inflation compatible with the paper's Planck-2018 comparison, admit scalar-field background correspondences, and satisfy the trans-Planckian censorship conjecture?

sources.title: Possible Theoretical limits on holographic quintessence from weak gravity conjecture

evidence.text: The proposed criterion asks whether the canonical scalar displacement needed to reproduce holographic dark energy remains at most one reduced Planck mass over a selected cosmological interval.

sources.title: Warm inflation with Barrow holographic dark energy

evidence.text: Can Barrow holographic dark energy (BHDE), interacting with radiation, drive warm inflation in a highly dissipative regime while satisfying slow-roll conditions and the observational bounds quoted in the paper?

sources.title: Holographic Naturalness and Cosmological Relaxation

evidence.text: Can a hidden holographic environment stabilize dark energy and inflation against Planck-scale radiative mixing, erase trans-Planckian modes, and supply an entropic criterion for cosmological evolution?

sources.title: Weak Gravity Conjecture and Holographic Dark Energy model with Interaction and Spatial Curvature

evidence.text: Can spatial curvature and phenomenological matter–dark-energy interactions allow holographic quintessence to satisfy the adopted sub-Planckian scalar-excursion criterion within the observational parameter regions used by the paper?

sources.title: Holographic dilatonic model of dark energy

evidence.text: Can a dilaton scalar effectively reproduce future-event-horizon holographic dark energy (HDE), with reconstructed kinetic evolution that supports acceleration and quantum stability?

sources.title: Barrow holographic dark energy interacting model in the presence of radiation and matter

evidence.text: How does interacting radiation change Barrow holographic dark energy evolution in open and closed universes, and what parameter constraints follow from CC+BAO and Pantheon+SH0ES fits?

destination.title: Consistency, interactions and probes of spinning-field EFTs
destination.question: How do interaction structure, consistency conditions and physical observables delimit effective descriptions of spinning fields?
destination.summary: The core concerns interaction-dependent cutoffs and consistency of massive spinning fields and gravitational amplitudes. Vector charge criteria, curved spin-2 settings, amplitude constructions and observational applications provide distinct directions. Entropy arguments and broader quantum-gravity reviews supply context rather than universal premises.

systems: Massive higher-spin particles, massive spin-2 fields and massive gravitons, distinguished source by source
Gravitational EFT amplitudes and selected bimetric or cosmological settings
targets: Perturbative validity scales, interaction constraints and possible additional spectra
Charge interpretation, amplitude construction and background-dependent consistency
regimes: Source-specific weak-coupling, scattering, compositeness and mass-gap assumptions
Flat-space and curved-background questions remain separate
Dimensions and perturbative orders are not shared family assumptions
assumptions: Conjectures and conditional source claims remain distinguishable from verified results
Ordinary EFT work remains eligible without a Swampland premise
conventions: A perturbative strong-coupling scale need not equal a required-new-state threshold
A massive graviton differs from an additional massive spin-2 field coupled to massless gravity
Gauge redundancy alone does not establish the physical charge required by a conjectural argument
includes: Separate access to construction, consistency, application and comparison questions
Massless higher-spin interactions as a changed-regime neighbor
excludes: A universal obstruction inferred from shared spin terminology
Automatic transfer of source-setting graph relations to every question
Atomic Lamb-shift bounds and geon statistics as direct evidence for massive higher-spin cutoff claims

sources.title: Universal bound on the strong coupling scale of a gravitationally coupled massive spin-2 particle

evidence.text: What is the greatest possible strong coupling scale for an isolated massive spin-2 particle coupled to Einstein gravity, allowing general local interactions? How does the answer change with wrong-sign kinetic terms, and what might generalize to higher spin?

sources.title: Natural selection rules: new positivity bounds for massive spinning particles

evidence.text: Can angular-momentum selection rules strengthen beyond-forward EFT positivity bounds for massive spinning particles, including constraints on lower-dimensional interactions under additional UV convergence assumptions?

sources.title: Supersymmetric Massive Gravity

evidence.text: Which cubic self-interactions of an isolated massive graviton admit supersymmetry, and how do these constraints connect to dRGT tuning, high-energy Galileon interactions and a massive double copy?

sources.title: Universal bound on the strong coupling scale of a gravitationally coupled massive spin-2 particle

evidence.text: Use transversity amplitudes, strip kinematic singularities, and tune polynomial contact terms to cancel high-energy exchange growth at fixed angle. Impose crossing and match to a polarization-tensor contact vertex to ensure little-group covariance. Raise the target scale until this construction fails.

sources.title: Natural selection rules: new positivity bounds for massive spinning particles

evidence.text: Expand helicity amplitudes in angular-momentum partial waves with Wigner rotation matrix elements. Combine the optical theorem with J≥|h_s| and bounds on angular-momentum matrix elements.

sources.title: Supersymmetric Massive Gravity

evidence.text: Use Lorentz-covariant massive spinor-helicity and on-shell superspace instead of an interacting off-shell action. Grassmann Fourier transforms and superspace translations solve supersymmetry Ward identities; Grassmann derivatives extract component amplitudes.

sources.title: Universal bound on the strong coupling scale of a gravitationally coupled massive spin-2 particle

evidence.text: Classify on-shell cubic vertices using contractions of momenta and auxiliary polarization vectors. Massive polarization tensors are symmetric, transverse and traceless. Identical-particle permutations, massless gauge invariance and dimension-dependent identities constrain the structures.

sources.title: Universal bound on the strong coupling scale of a gravitationally coupled massive spin-2 particle

evidence.text: Construct exchange amplitudes from cubic vertices and propagators, then add general local quartic contact terms. The quartic tensor representation has 201 structures with polynomial Mandelstam coefficients; these structures have further dependencies in four dimensions.

sources.title: Natural selection rules: new positivity bounds for massive spinning particles

evidence.text: Remove unphysical kinematic singularities using a spin/helicity-dependent regulated amplitude. Apply fixed-t Cauchy dispersion relations to its even s derivatives, subtracting EFT poles and cuts through scale μ.

sources.title: Islands and light gravitons in type IIB string theory

evidence.text: Can quantum extremal islands coexist with a quantitatively controlled light graviton and a valid massive-gravity EFT in type IIB embeddings, and how does dilaton variation change their zero- and finite-temperature behavior?

sources.title: Spin-2 fields and the weak gravity conjecture

evidence.text: How do two interacting metric sectors distribute their kinetic normalization between massless and massive spin-2 eigenstates?

sources.title: Bootstrapping the chiral-gravitational anomaly

evidence.text: What restrictions do analyticity, unitarity, and crossing impose on a U(1)-gravitational anomaly coupling, and at what scale must higher-spin states enter an effective theory containing its pseudo-Goldstone boson and gravitons?

sources.title: Entropy Constraints on High Spin Particles

evidence.text: Does the information attributed to spin degeneracy constrain arbitrarily high-spin elementary particles through the Bekenstein bound, and what additional length scales arise with and without gravity?

sources.title: Effective field theory of Stückelberg vector bosons

evidence.text: Which leading interactions can a massive Stückelberg vector have without an associated physical gauge symmetry, and how do its longitudinal couplings determine observable energy growth and the EFT cutoff?

sources.title: Positive Signs in Massive Gravity

evidence.text: What restrictions do unitary, analytic graviton scattering amplitudes impose on ghost-free massive gravity, and can the full massive-spin-2 theory avoid the forward-positivity obstruction of its isolated Galileon limit?

sources.title: A Model Independent Ultraviolet Cutoff for Theories with Charged Massive Higher Spin Fields

evidence.text: What model-independent upper bound limits the ultraviolet cutoff of a local theory containing an electromagnetically charged massive higher-spin particle, and how does it depend parametrically on mass, spin, and charge?

sources.title: Rescuing Massive Photons from the Swampland

evidence.text: Must consistency conditions imposed on a higher-energy compact gauge theory retain their original form in an infrared theory containing a light massive vector?

sources.title: Higuchi Bound on Slow Roll Inflation and the Swampland

evidence.text: The setting supplies a nonlinear effective description of one massive and one massless gravitating spin-two field. Coupling matter to one metric fixes which cosmic time, stress tensor, and observable Hubble parameter enter the subsequent calculation.

sources.title: The simplest massive S-matrix: from minimal coupling to Black Holes

evidence.text: What physical systems realize the simplest massive three-point amplitude, and how do its electromagnetic and gravitational couplings determine Compton amplitudes and classical spinning-black-hole interactions?

sources.title: Spin-2 fields and the weak gravity conjecture

evidence.text: Can an interacting massive spin-2 particle remain isolated below a much higher EFT cutoff, despite the tower needed in known weakly coupled completions?

sources.title: Regge growth of isolated massive spin-2 particles and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can an isolated massive spin-2 particle coupled to gravity have tree-level elastic scattering growing no faster than s² in a Regge window below the EFT cutoff?

sources.title: Gravitational effective field theory islands, low-spin dominance, and the four-graviton amplitude

evidence.text: How tightly do perturbative unitarity, crossing and dispersive constraints restrict leading four-dimensional gravitational EFT corrections? Can low-spin dominance explain why explicit theories occupy much smaller coupling regions, and can different helicities constrain the R³ coupling?

sources.title: Causality Constraints on Corrections to the Graviton Three-Point Coupling

evidence.text: Does asymptotic causality constrain non-Einstein graviton three-point couplings before gravity becomes strongly coupled, and link their characteristic length scales to new higher-spin states?

sources.title: Massive gravity is not positive

evidence.text: Can dRGT massive gravity describe a parametrically broad energy interval above graviton mass m while satisfying finite-momentum-transfer positivity, and can detuned potentials, higher derivatives or non-gravitational spin-2 interactions evade the resulting restriction?

sources.title: From Swampland to Phenomenology and Back

evidence.text: Can a light massive Abelian gauge field remain a valid effective theory up to a high ultraviolet cutoff? The example uses a Stückelberg compensator so that a photon mass is compatible with the displayed U(1) gauge redundancy.

sources.title: (Super) gravity from positivity

evidence.text: Can an interacting massive spin-3/2 particle have a weakly coupled EFT with a large mass gap while satisfying causality and unitarity? Do positivity constraints require gravity, supersymmetric couplings, and gauging of a Dirac particle's U(1)?

sources.title: A Spin‐2 Conjecture on the Swampland

evidence.text: The starting model isolates the helicity-1 sector of a massive spin-2 particle coupled to Einstein gravity. The five massive polarizations are organized into two tensor, two vector and one scalar degrees of freedom.

sources.title: Ultraviolet-infrared bounds and minimum coupling in effective field theories

evidence.text: Can the requirement that a gauge interaction be physically distinguishable from a global symmetry impose a minimum coupling when an EFT has related ultraviolet and infrared cutoffs? How do entropy, black-hole exclusion and the number of degrees of freedom affect that bound?

sources.title: Probing higher-spin particles with gravitational waves from compact binary inspirals

evidence.text: Can compact-binary inspiral waveforms constrain gravitationally coupled higher-spin particles through their low-energy gravitational EFT imprint, without specifying a detailed dark-sector model?

sources.title: Higher Spin Supersymmetry at the Cosmological Collider: Sculpting SUSY Rilles in the CMB

evidence.text: What angular signatures do massive higher-spin fermions and their supersymmetric partners produce in primordial scalar and tensor-scalar-scalar three-point functions?

sources.title: A Species or Weak-Gravity Bound for Large $N$ Gauge Theories Coupled to Gravity

evidence.text: When do gravitational causality constraints on massive higher-spin particles apply to composites, and what bounds follow for confining large N gauge theories coupled to Einstein gravity?

sources.title: Stringy Completions of the Standard Model from the Bottom Up

evidence.text: Can a specified soft, weakly coupled four-point completion accommodate gravitational, gauge, and scalar interactions with consistent massive-state exchange?

sources.title: Higher spin gauge theories in four-dimensions, three-dimensions, and two-dimensions

evidence.text: How can interacting massless higher-spin fields preserve their gauge symmetries, including gravitational and matter couplings? The talk reviews four- and three-dimensional results and introduces a two-dimensional matter-interaction model.

sources.title: Closed Strings and Weak Gravity from Higher-Spin Causality

evidence.text: When can stable or metastable massive higher-spin particles couple causally to gravity, and what bounds follow on the gravitational higher-spin scale, nongravitational interactions, and a weakly coupled UV completion?

sources.title: Massive Spin-2 Scattering and Asymptotic Superluminality

evidence.text: What constraints does absence of a measurable asymptotic time advance impose on an isolated massive spin-2 particle's cubic interactions, and when must new physics enter if those constraints fail?

sources.title: The Swampland Conjectures: A Bridge from Quantum Gravity to Particle Physics

evidence.text: Can an experimentally tiny Stückelberg photon mass coexist with a high-cutoff gravitational EFT?

sources.title: A Spin‐2 Conjecture on the Swampland

evidence.text: The strong version asks whether a graviton itself can be massive while remaining in a finite-field effective description above its mass.

sources.title: Spin-2 fields and the weak gravity conjecture

evidence.text: Why can a Stückelberg formulation of a massive vector retain the physical charge needed by the WGC?
